newsitem.title: INDIA: India signs deals for 275,000 T soymeal exports.
newsitem.headline: India signs deals for 275,000 T soymeal exports.

text.p: Indian exporters have signed contracts for nearly 275,000 tonnes of soymeal exports for November-December shipments and expect prices to further firm up, traders said on Tuesday.
"There is a steady upward trend in soymeal prices," said Davish Jain, chairman of the Soybean Processors Association of India (SOPA).
"Traders are waiting for new developments and exporters are looking for better prices."
Traders said overseas deals for around 100,000 tonnes of soymeal were signed at $238-250 per tonne f.a.s. while another 100,000 tonnes were sold at $250-270.
Contracts for the remaining 75,000 tonnes were signed at $270-278 per tonne.
Soymeal export prices for the new crop were currently ruling at $278 per tonne compared to $205-206 in the previous year. Soymeal for September-October shipment was quoted at $292-293 per tonne.
Traders said fresh soybean arrivals in the western state of Maharashtra were quoted at around 13,150 rupees per tonne.
Harvesting had not begun in the central state of Madhya Pradesh, which accounts for nearly 80 percent of the country's soybean output.
